title: Your first real render
goal: You will create and render a smooth colored sphere on a floor with materials, lighting, a camera, and finished render settings.
prerequisites: A mouse with a scroll wheel or middle button

steps.where: Center 3D Viewport, using the selected cube and the X keyboard shortcut.
steps.why: This clears space for the model you will create.
steps.checkpoint: The cube disappears, while Camera and Light remain listed in the Outliner at the top-right.
hint_levels: Look for the orange-outlined cube in the center.
Select only the cube before using Blender's delete command.
Left-click the cube, press X, then press Enter.

steps.where: 3D Viewport header > Add menu > Mesh submenu.
steps.why: The sphere will be the main model in the finished image.
steps.checkpoint: A sphere appears at the center and Sphere is listed in the Outliner.
hint_levels: Open the Add menu above the 3D Viewport.
The rounded object is inside the Mesh submenu.
Click Add > Mesh > UV Sphere.

steps.action: Move the sphere upward by one meter.
steps.where: 3D Viewport, using the G and Z keyboard shortcuts.
steps.why: Raising the sphere places its bottom on the future floor.
steps.checkpoint: The sphere sits above the red X-axis and its Z location is 1 m in the Item panel.
hint_levels: Constrain the movement to the vertical blue axis.
Start Grab, choose the Z axis, and enter a precise distance.
With the sphere selected, press G, press Z, type 1, then press Enter.

steps.action: Apply smooth shading to the sphere.
steps.where: Object menu in the 3D Viewport header.
steps.why: Smooth shading removes the visibly faceted look from the model.
steps.checkpoint: The sphere's surface looks visually smooth instead of polygonal.
hint_levels: Look for a shading command in the Object menu.
The command is named Shade Auto Smooth in current Blender versions.
With the sphere selected, click Object > Shade Auto Smooth.

steps.action: Add a plane at the world origin.
steps.where: 3D Viewport header > Add menu > Mesh submenu.
steps.why: The plane provides a floor that can receive light and shadows.
steps.checkpoint: A flat square appears beneath the sphere and Plane is listed in the Outliner.
hint_levels: Return to the Add menu used for the sphere.
Choose the flat primitive from the Mesh submenu.
Click Add > Mesh > Plane.

steps.action: Scale the plane to ten times its original size.
steps.where: 3D Viewport, using the S keyboard shortcut.
steps.why: A larger floor fills the camera view around the model.
steps.checkpoint: The plane extends well beyond the sphere in every horizontal direction.
hint_levels: Use Blender's Scale command while the plane is selected.
Enter a number after pressing S for an exact uniform scale.
With Plane selected, press S, type 10, then press Enter.

steps.action: Give the sphere a blue material.
steps.where: Right-side Properties editor > Material Properties tab > Surface section > Base Color.
steps.why: A colored material makes the model respond visibly to the scene lighting.
steps.checkpoint: In Material Preview mode, the sphere appears blue while the plane remains gray.
hint_levels: Select Sphere in the Outliner, then find the red checker-sphere Material Properties icon.
Create a material with New, then change its Principled BSDF Base Color.
Select Sphere, click Material Properties > New > Base Color, choose blue, then click outside the color picker.

steps.action: Give the plane a light-gray material.
steps.where: Right-side Properties editor > Material Properties tab > Surface section > Base Color.
steps.why: A neutral floor contrasts with the blue model and keeps its shadow readable.
steps.checkpoint: In Material Preview mode, the floor appears light gray and the sphere remains blue.
hint_levels: Select the floor before creating its separate material.
Use the same New and Base Color controls you used for the sphere.
Select Plane in the Outliner, click Material Properties > New > Base Color, choose light gray, then click outside the color picker.

steps.action: Increase the existing light's power to 1200 watts.
steps.where: Outliner > Light, then right-side Properties editor > Object Data Properties tab > Light > Power.
steps.why: A stronger light clearly illuminates the model and creates a visible shadow.
steps.checkpoint: The Power field reads 1200 W and Rendered viewport shading shows a brighter sphere and floor.
hint_levels: Select Light in the Outliner and look for its green light-bulb properties icon.
The Power field is near the top of the Light data settings.
Click Light in the Outliner > Object Data Properties > Power, type 1200, then press Enter.

steps.action: Set the camera to Location X 7, Y -7, Z 5 and Rotation X 68°, Y 0°, Z 46°.
steps.where: Outliner > Camera, then 3D Viewport right sidebar > Item tab > Transform section.
steps.why: These transforms aim the camera toward the sphere and floor from an elevated angle.
steps.checkpoint: Pressing Numpad 0 shows the sphere and surrounding floor inside the camera frame.
hint_levels: Select Camera and open its numeric Transform controls.
Use the Location and Rotation fields in the Item tab, including the minus sign for Y Location.
Select Camera, press N, open Item > Transform, enter Location 7, -7, 5 and Rotation 68°, 0°, 46°, then press Numpad 0.

steps.action: Set the output resolution to 800 by 800 pixels at 100 percent.
steps.where: Right-side Properties editor > Output Properties tab > Format section.
steps.why: A square output creates a manageable final image with predictable dimensions.
steps.checkpoint: Resolution X reads 800 px, Y reads 800 px, and Percentage reads 100%.
hint_levels: Look for the printer-shaped Output Properties icon.
The image dimensions are in the Format section under Resolution.
Open Output Properties > Format and set Resolution X to 800, Y to 800, and Percentage to 100%.

steps.where: Top menu bar > Render menu > Render Image command.
steps.why: Rendering combines the model, materials, light, camera, and output settings into the final image.
steps.checkpoint: The Render Result window shows a blue sphere on a light-gray floor with illumination and a visible shadow.
hint_levels: The final command is in the Render menu at the top.
Choose Render Image and wait while Blender calculates the frame.
Click Render > Render Image, or press F12, and wait for Render Result to appear.
